Both configurations. For standalone PoC with a USB PSU, use two USB outputs with at least 1 A combined rated capacity and adequate per-port ratings: one to Nano, one through the barrel cable to J0 for the LED branch. Alternatively power Nano from PC USB and LEDs from the separate regulated 5 V PSU. Best practice also powers U1. Minimum uses J0 to feed only the lower-right +5 V and GND rails. Grounds join; do not join independent +5 V feeds through Nano headers. Check actual PSU label, output connector, and lead polarity. Current rating is available capacity, not current forced into the load.

description: 64-row solderless breadboard and suitable jumper wires
notes: Both configurations. Standard a-e and f-j terminal banks, separated by the centre gap. Best practice: both + rails carry 5 V and both - rails GND; bridge all four midpoint breaks and link left/right rails as drawn. Minimum: only lower-right + and - rail segments are used, with no bridges or rail-pair links. Only a physically short LED section belongs on these power contacts.

description: APA102 LED strip; 160 inches planned, 60 LEDs per metre
notes: Both configurations. Start with 1-5 physically connected pixels; five pixels are about 8.3 cm and allow a conservative 0.30 A LED budget at 60 mA/pixel, plus the Nano/buffer on their branches. Connect the INPUT end: a40 GND, a41 CI, a42 DI, a43 +5 V. CO/DO are downstream outputs. Cut only at marked pads. Minimum omits the buffer and all resistors/capacitors; direct 3.3 V control may not work with the particular strip.

description: Power distribution and supply sized for the complete APA102 strip
notes: 160 inches = 4.064 m, about 244 pixels at 60/m. A conservative 60 mA/pixel planning value gives about 14.6 A at 5 V before controller draw; actual variant/current must be checked. Full-strip power needs suitable external wiring and injection, not the breadboard or Nano USB path. Guide: https://learn.adafruit.com/adafruit-dotstar-leds/power-and-connections
